title: Harbor and Letter
premise: In the river port of Vessing, Bram Thornbury has survived twelve years of indenture to the Corvane Trading Company by being useful and unremarkable. When a drowned courier's sealed letter surfaces in a net—naming the Thornburys as sworn guarantors of a debt owed by Kestrel Marrow, now branded an enemy of the Company—Bram learns their late father promised protection in peacetime that the law now forbids keeping. As the ice on the Vessing River thaws, Bram must smuggle proof of the Company's own forged ledgers to Kestrel before the spring tribunal, trading invisibility for justice that no court will grant. The book ends with Bram delivering the letter and testimony at the water's edge as the ice breaks, choosing exile with Kestrel over a life built on silence.
about_author: Tamsin Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping manifests and indenture records from forgotten port towns. Harbor and Letter is their second novel, drawn from a single marginal note found in a ledger: 'promised, in peacetime.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A day in the life of a diver for the Corvane Company: hauling oysters, mending nets, staying small. We learn the indenture terms, the harbor's rhythms, and Bram's habit of memorizing everything while appearing to notice nothing. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Net Brought Up
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A drowned courier tangles in Bram's net, clutching a wax-sealed letter addressed to 'the Thornbury name.' Fearful of the Company's harbor watch, Bram hides it rather than surrender it. That night they break the seal and find their family named as guarantor. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, shifting between memory and present. Investigating quietly, Bram discovers the courier was carrying evidence that Corvane's ledgers were forged to brand Kestrel Marrow an enemy—and that the forgery implicates the harbormaster. Emotional beat: the first taste of righteous anger.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, told through recovered letters from their father. Flashbacks reveal the wartime pact: the Thornburys sheltered Kestrel's fleet, and he swore to answer any call they made. Bram realizes the letter is that call, arriving years too late. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Eye
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Bram and Odile Vash, the harbormaster's sharp-eyed clerk who suspects Bram knows more than she should. Odile offers quiet warning—or is it a trap? Bram must decide whether anyone in power can be trusted. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a rope.

chapters.title: Salt and Snowmelt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With the river still frozen, Bram seeks out old allies—a defrocked priest, a smuggler aunt—to plan the crossing to Kestrel's stronghold before the tribunal convenes at ice-break. Each ally demands a price. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; Bram stops being invisible.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Summons
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Company summons all indentured workers to testify against Kestrel; refusal means the whipping post. Odile, torn, slips Bram a copy of the witness list—and finds her own name on it. Emotional beat: complicity cracking into conscience.

chapters.title: Crossing the Black Ice
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Under cover of a February fog, Bram crosses the frozen river with the forged ledger pages sewn into their coat, pursued by Company riders. The ice groans and splits early; Bram nearly drowns but reaches Kestrel's camp. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration—the point of no return.

chapters.title: Enemy at the Water's Edge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Bram and Kestrel Marrow. Kestrel, hardened and suspicious, tests Bram's claim before accepting the evidence. Together they plan to confront the tribunal not with violence but with the ledgers themselves, read aloud before the whole harbor. Emotional beat: trust kindled between strangers bound by a dead man's word.

chapters.title: When the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with Odile's final testimony woven in. At the spring tribunal, Bram reads the forged entries aloud as the river cracks and roars behind them; the crowd turns, the harbormaster falls, and the Company's writ fractures. Bram, indenture voided, chooses exile aboard Kestrel's ship. Emotional beat: liberation bought at the cost of belonging—justice outside the law, kept inside a promise.
